papers.title: Effects of Alfv\'enicity on the Compressible Energy Cascade in Magnetohydrodynamic Solar Wind Turbulence: Evidence from Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter, and WIND observations
papers.abstract: The compressible MHD energy cascade in the solar wind is shaped by Alfv\'enicity, plasma fluctuations, and proton temperature, yet how these factors regulate the relative weight of compressible and incompressible energy transfer across heliocentric distances remains poorly understood. We apply compressible and incompressible exact relations to a large sample of 2-hour intervals from WIND (1~au), Parker Solar Probe ($<0.25$~au), and Solar Orbiter (0.3--1~au), classifying intervals as Alfv\'enic ($|\sigma_c|>0.75$) or non-Alfv\'enic ($|\sigma_c|<0.25$) and by wind speed, and examine the Yaglom-like and purely compressible components of the compressible cascade. Velocity fluctuation amplitude is the strongest predictor of the compressible cascade rate $\langle|\varepsilon_c|\rangle$, followed by density and magnetic field fluctuations. $\langle|\varepsilon_c|\rangle$ and $\langle|\varepsilon_i|\rangle$ are tightly correlated in all regimes, with their ratio organized by Alfv\'enicity and wind speed: non-Alfv\'enic and Alfv\'enic fast winds cluster along $\langle|\varepsilon_c|\rangle=\langle|\varepsilon_i|\rangle$, while Alfv\'enic slow wind shows a systematic excess consistent with internal energy contributions. The largest $\langle|\varepsilon_c|\rangle$ systematically occur in hotter intervals, with a two-decade increase from cool to hot events in Alfv\'enic slow and non-Alfv\'enic wind, a trend carried mainly by the purely compressible term, while the dominant Yaglom-like term controls the overall cascade magnitude. Alfv\'enicity and wind speed thus govern the efficiency of turbulent energy transfer across heliocentric distances, and the tight coupling between compressible and incompressible rates points to the need for compressible, multi-fluid descriptions of the solar wind dissipation budget.

papers.title: The Dst index - empirical fits and temporal correlations
papers.abstract: Here I show how it is possible to make an empirical fit of yearly sets of Dst index values to the log-normal distribution, using the Kullback-Liebler divergence to test each fit performance. Further, since any real sequence of Dst values contains correlation with the near-past, I also compute autocorrelations in order to understand the timescales over which it retains memory.

papers.title: Detection and Statistics of large-scale Sector Boundary Crossings in the Solar Wind: The SBCross Catalog
papers.abstract: Heliospheric sector boundary crossings (SBCs), composed of the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS), Heliospheric Plasma Sheet (HPS), and surrounding plasma halo, represent fundamental structures in the solar wind that influence interplanetary dynamics and space weather. We present the \textsc{SBCross} catalog, an automated, publicly available database containing 1,076 SBC events derived from in-situ observations spanning more than 30 years (1995--2026), covering Solar Cycles 23 and 24 alongside the rising and maximum phases of Solar Cycle 25. By combining interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) and 255~eV suprathermal electron pitch angle distributions (PAD) data, our algorithm reliably captures large-scale polarity transitions, with $76\%$ of detected SBCs exhibiting clear HPS signatures ($\beta > 1$, $n_{\mathrm{peak}} > 10\mathrm{\,cm^{-3}}$). Across the catalog, we find an average occurrence rate of $\approx 2.6$ events per Carrington rotation, a median event duration of $\approx 9.0$\,hours, and a median physical thickness of $\approx 7.4 \times 10^6$\,km. Furthermore, approximately $\approx 15\%$ of detected SBCs interact with interplanetary coronal mass ejections (CMEs) on average, with this proportion rising up to $33\%$ during solar maximum. These CME-associated events exhibit systematically longer durations (median of $10.0$\,hours), $54\%$ larger physical thicknesses, and higher average solar wind velocities. Notably, all high-velocity SBC events ($> 600\mathrm{\,km\,s^{-1}}$) are exclusively driven by CME interactions, demonstrating local plasma pile-up and structural entanglement resulting from fast CMEs overtaking the ambient slow background. The \textsc{SBCross} catalog serves as an updated successor to the classic SBC list by L. Svalgaard, delivering a standardized, open-access resource for the heliophysics community to systematically investigate sector boundary transitions.
